newsitem.title: USA: Waste Management sets contract with CEO.
newsitem.headline: Waste Management sets contract with CEO.

text.p: Waste Management Inc. said Friday it signed a five-year contract with Ronald LeMay, granting the recently named chairman, president and chief executive officer an annual salary of $1.5 million.
In July, LeMay resigned as president and chief operating officer of Sprint Corp. to head the world's largest provider of comprehensive waste management services.

LeMay's contract also calls for annual cash incentive compensation targeted at 80 percent of his base salary. This award will depend on the company's ability to reach performance goals under its economic value added programme.

Because LeMay is forfeiting his annual incentive award from Sprint, Waste Management guaranteed an incentive award of $1 million for 1997. He is also guaranteed awards of $350,000 for 1998 and $250,000 for 1999 because he forfeited long-term incentive awards from Sprint,
Waste Management's long-term incentive plan is linked to total stockholder return over successive three-year periods.

The contract also calls for option grants to buy 500,000 shares of Waste Management stock in each of four years beginning in April 1998. The strike price will be equal to the fair market value of the Oak Brook, Ill.-based company's stock at the time the options are issued.

Waste Management said that in addition to salary, incentive compensation and stock options, LeMay's contract also provides for sign-on incentives to leave Sprint and replace compensation he forfeited.

These incentives include an award of 353,000 restricted shares of Waste Management stock, vesting at a rate of 20 percent a year; a grant of 10-year options to purchase a total of 2 million shares of Waste Management stock at a strike price of $33.10 a share, and stock appreciation rights.

The company said LeMay resigned his positions on the boards of directors of Mercantile Bank of Kansas City and Imation Corp. He is limiting his outside board memberships to Yellow Corp. and Ceridian Corp.
Waste Management's stock fell 31 cents to $32.31 on the New York Stock Exchange.
